lineage_context.teaching_goal: Use the single project Symplocos concept to teach alternate exstipulate leaves, many epipetalous stamens, inferior ovary and a persistent-calyx drupe.

project_scope.note: The project has one genus and one species, so the family lesson deliberately leans on the precise FNA reproductive package rather than pretending to show broader family variation.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: On a woody plant with alternate simple leaves, inspect the flower center: Symplocaceae typically has dozens of stamens attached to the corolla, an inferior ovary, and a drupaceous fruit crowned by the persistent calyx.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Shrubs or trees; leaves alternate, simple, exstipulate, usually with glandular teeth or obscure crenulations.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers usually 5-part and sympetalous; nectary disk present; stamens very numerous, commonly about 40–100, epipetalous and often grouped in fascicles; ovary inferior and incompletely locular.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Drupe, typically crowned by the persistent calyx.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: For local sweetleaf, the strongest package is alternate simple leaf + many stamens + inferior ovary + persistent-calyx drupe.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: leaf margin → flower before leaves → many stamens → inferior ovary → drupe
visual_lesson.intro: Symplocaceae looks ordinary vegetatively, but the flower center is anything but ordinary: dozens of stamens crowd around a single style above an inferior ovary.

steps.title: 1 · Read the leaf and bud context
steps.look_for: Alternate simple leaves with obscure crenulate-serrulate to nearly entire margins and prominent midvein.
steps.why_it_matters: Establishes the woody sweetleaf gestalt before flowering.

steps.title: 2 · Catch the flowers before the leaves
steps.look_for: Creamy yellow flowers in axillary fascicles from previous-year wood, often appearing before new leaves.

steps.title: 3 · Count 'many,' not five
steps.look_for: Numerous stamens, often dozens, attached to the corolla and grouped around the style.
steps.why_it_matters: Separates Symplocaceae from many other 5-part woody Ericales.

steps.title: 4 · Confirm inferior ovary and drupe
steps.look_for: Inferior ovary maturing into a dark orange-brown drupe with persistent calyx at the top.

comparisons.title: Symplocaceae vs Styracaceae
comparisons.rule: Symplocaceae has very numerous epipetalous stamens and drupaceous fruit; project Styracaceae has fewer stamens and dry winged/capsular fruit.

comparisons.title: Symplocaceae vs Sapotaceae
comparisons.rule: Both are woody and can have fused flowers, but Sapotaceae has latex plus a hard glossy seed; Symplocaceae emphasizes many stamens, inferior ovary and persistent-calyx drupe.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not use sweetness/taste as a crew ID test; use visible leaf, flower and fruit characters.

genera.fast_cue: alternate simple leaves + early axillary flower fascicles + many stamens + persistent-calyx drupe

visual_targets.annotation_goal: show previous-year twig and axillary fascicle

curation_status.family_backfill_phase: recognition module built; species promotion independent
